The test image shows a corn leaf with a classic mosaic pattern: irregular patches of light green/yellow and dark green, with narrow streaks along the leaf veins. This is the hallmark of Maize dwarf mosaic virus. Key distinguishing features:
- Mosaic mottling (not distinct stripes like downy mildew)
- No water-soaked lesions or freckles (rules out Goss's wilt)
- No vein banding/clearing pattern (rules out MCDV)
- No stunting or reddening visible (rules out Corn Stunt)
